title: Extracting High-Molecular Weight DNA from Cyanobacteria Using Promega's Wizard HMW DNA Kit
author: Hept, Greene
materials: Promega Wizard HMW DNA extraction kit

steps.title: Harvest and split culture
steps.instruction: Take at least 75 mL stationary‑phase cyanobacterial culture and split it into two 50 mL centrifuge tubes.

steps.title: Centrifuge cells
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the two 50 mL tubes at 16,000 × g for 10 min in a microcentrifuge; discard the supernatant and keep the pellets.

steps.title: Resuspend and combine pellets
steps.instruction: Add 1 mL deionized water to one pellet, mix, then transfer this suspension to the other tube containing its pellet, mix again, and move the combined suspension to a 2 mL microcentrifuge tube.

steps.title: Initial spin and PBS wash
steps.instruction: Spin the 2 mL tube for 3 min at 16,000 × g, remove the supernatant, add 100 µL PBS, and resuspend the pellet.

steps.title: Add HMW Lysis Buffer A
steps.instruction: Add 500 µL HMW Lysis Buffer A using a 1,000 µL wide‑bore tip; mix gently five times by a slow draw‑up followed by a rapid, controlled expulsion down the side of the tube.

steps.title: Heat lysate
steps.instruction: Incubate the lysate at 80 °C for 6 min, then allow it to cool to room temperature; the solution should change from dark vibrant green to dull pale green.

steps.title: RNase A treatment
steps.instruction: Add 3 µL RNase A solution, invert the tube gently seven times, and incubate at 37 °C for 15 min.

steps.title: Proteinase K digestion
steps.instruction: Add 20 µL Proteinase K solution, invert gently ten times, incubate at 56 °C for 15 min, then chill on ice for 1 min.

steps.title: Protein precipitation
steps.instruction: Add 200 µL Protein Precipitation Solution, mix gently five times with a wide‑bore 1,000 µL tip (slow draw‑up, rapid expulsion), and incubate on ice for 5 min.

steps.title: Prepare wide-bore tips
steps.instruction: If wide‑bore tips are unavailable, cut regular pipette tips to resemble wide‑bore tips; do not vortex.

steps.title: Extended centrifugation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 16,000 × g for 15 min. If darker green wisps of mucilage remain, respin for an additional 5 min or longer until the pellet is tightly packed. The pellet should appear dark green; the supernatant should be light green with no visible clumps.

steps.title: Transfer supernatant to isopropanol
steps.instruction: Using a wide‑bore 1,000 µL tip, carefully aspirate the green supernatant (avoiding the pellet) and dispense it into a new tube that already contains 600 µL isopropanol. Have 10 mL isopropanol, 200 µL regular tips, and two 200 µL pipettes ready.

steps.title: Mix isopropanol mixture
steps.instruction: Gently invert the tube 8 times and incubate for 1 min; a DNA pellet should begin to unravel and become visible.

steps.title: Iterative isopropanol replacement
steps.instruction: Using a 200 µL tip, carefully withdraw up to 200 µL of the green supernatant and replace it with 200 µL fresh isopropanol. Repeat this wash‑replace cycle until the solution is clear and virtually no mucilage remains.

steps.title: Pellet DNA
steps.instruction: After the supernatant is clear, centrifuge the tube for 2 min at 16,000 × g; a visible DNA pellet should be present.

steps.title: Ethanol wash
steps.instruction: Decant the supernatant, add 600 µL 70 % ethanol, gently invert the tube 7 times, and centrifuge again for 2 min at 16,000 × g.

steps.title: Air-dry DNA pellet
steps.instruction: Carefully decant the ethanol, invert the tube onto clean absorbent paper, and allow the pellet to air‑dry for 15 min.

steps.title: Rehydrate DNA
steps.instruction: Add 200 µL DNA Rehydration Solution, incubate for 1 h at 65 °C, tapping the tube gently every 15 min to mix.

steps.title: Homogenize and store DNA
steps.instruction: If the pellet has dissolved, gently mix the solution with a wide‑bore 200 µL tip until homogeneous, then store the DNA at 4 °C for 24 h before quantification, concentration, or agarose‑gel analysis.
